source.title: Delta Dental Plan Understanding Document
source.network: Delta Dental PPO plus Premier Network

qa.question: What network does the dental plan use?
qa.answer: Delta Dental PPO plus Premier Network.

qa.question: Is there an office visit copayment?
qa.answer: None.

qa.question: What does Coverage A (Diagnostic / Preventive) pay?
qa.answer: Delta Dental pays 100%; no waiting period; no deductible.

qa.question: What does Coverage B (Basic Restorative) pay?
qa.answer: Delta Dental pays 80%; no waiting period; calendar-year deductible $50 per person / $150 per family.

qa.question: What does Coverage C (Major Restorative) pay?
qa.answer: Delta Dental pays 50%; no waiting period; no deductible shown in the Coverage C column.

qa.question: What does Coverage D (Orthodontics) pay?
qa.answer: Delta Dental pays 50%; no waiting period; no deductible shown in the Coverage D column.

qa.question: What is the calendar-year maximum?
qa.answer: $1,500 per person, potentially up to $3,000 per person with Double-Up Max.

qa.question: What is the orthodontic lifetime maximum?
qa.answer: $1,500 per person.

qa.question: Is domestic partner coverage included?
qa.answer: Not included.

qa.question: Does the plan include any additional program?
qa.answer: Health through Oral Wellness® included.

qa.question: How are the benefit percentages calculated?
qa.answer: Benefit percentages are based on actual charges submitted up to the Maximum Allowable Charge for participating dentists, or Delta Dental’s allowance for non-participating dentists.

qa.question: What is covered under Coverage A (Diagnostic / Preventive), and how often?
qa.answer:
Coverage A (100%):
• Evaluations twice in a 12-month period, including periodic, limited, problem-focused, and comprehensive evaluations.
• Complete-series or panoramic x-rays once in a 5-year period.
• Bitewing x-rays once in a 12-month period.
• Individual-tooth x-rays as necessary.
• Brush biopsy once in a 12-month period.
• Two cleanings in a 12-month period.
• Fluoride once in a 12-month period through age 19.
• Space maintainers through age 16.
• Sealants on permanent molars once every 3 years per tooth for children through age 19.

qa.question: What is covered under Coverage B (Basic Restorative)?
qa.answer:
Coverage B (80%):
• Amalgam (silver) fillings and resin restorations.
• Surgical and routine extractions.
• Root canal therapy.
• Periodontal maintenance (cleaning).
• Treatment of gum disease.
• Clinical crown lengthening once per tooth per lifetime.
• Repair of a removable denture to its original condition.
• Emergency palliative treatment.

qa.question: What is covered under Coverage C (Major Restorative)?
qa.answer:
Coverage C (50%):
• Removable and fixed partial dentures (bridges), and complete dentures.
• Denture rebase and reline.
• Crowns.
• Onlays.
• Implants.

qa.question: What is covered under Coverage D (Orthodontics)?
qa.answer:
Coverage D (50%):
• Correction of malposed (crooked) teeth for dependent children and adults.
• If the plan includes an office visit copayment, that copayment does not apply to orthodontic services. This particular outline states the office visit copayment is none.

qa.question: How many cleanings can I get?
qa.answer: Cleanings are limited to two in a 12-month period. The two may be routine cleanings under Coverage A, periodontal cleanings under Coverage B, or a combination of both.

qa.question: Do diagnostic and preventive expenses count toward the annual maximum?
qa.answer: Covered diagnostic and preventive expenses also count toward the annual maximum; they are not excluded from that maximum.

qa.question: How often are x-rays covered?
qa.answer: Complete-series or panoramic x-rays once in a 5-year period. Bitewing x-rays once in a 12-month period. Individual-tooth x-rays as necessary.

qa.question: Is a root canal covered?
qa.answer: Root canal therapy is covered under Coverage B — Basic Restorative (80%).

qa.question: Are crowns covered?
qa.answer: Crowns are covered under Coverage C — Major Restorative (50%).

qa.question: Are implants covered?
qa.answer: Implants are covered under Coverage C — Major Restorative (50%).

qa.question: Are fillings covered?
qa.answer: Amalgam (silver) fillings and resin restorations are covered under Coverage B — Basic Restorative (80%).

qa.question: What is the deductible?
qa.answer: Coverage A has no deductible. The stated calendar-year deductible for Coverage B is $50 per person or $150 per family. The outline separately displays “No Deductible” for the other applicable plan columns; verify the detailed Dental Plan Description for exact allocation by service category.

qa.question: Are there waiting periods?
qa.answer: The listed categories show no waiting period. Any applicable waiting period is waived for employees and dependents who were covered immediately before the original effective date when this plan replaces an existing group dental policy that included the relevant services. New enrollees who become effective after the group’s original effective date are subject to waiting periods unless they move from one Northeast Delta Dental plan to this Northeast Delta Dental plan with no more than a one-month coverage gap. Waiting periods do not apply to eligible enrollees under age 19, except for orthodontic benefits.

qa.question: What is the lifetime maximum?
qa.answer: $1,500 per person, shown in the plan outline in connection with orthodontic coverage.

qa.question: What is Double-Up Max?
qa.answer: The plan allows an enrollee to double the calendar-year maximum by earning an additional $250 each year for use in future benefit periods. The carryover accumulates for each qualifying year up to an amount equal to the plan’s original calendar-year maximum.

qa.question: How do I qualify for the Double-Up Max carryover?
qa.answer: The enrollee must have a claim paid for an oral exam or a cleaning during the calendar year, demonstrating a focus on prevention. The enrollee’s total paid claims must not exceed $500 during that same calendar year.

qa.question: Does Double-Up Max apply to orthodontics?
qa.answer: The feature does not apply to orthodontic benefits.

qa.question: When does Double-Up Max start for groups that became effective mid-year?
qa.answer: Groups first effective from July through December begin qualifying for carryover in the following calendar year, for benefit dollars usable in the subsequent year.

qa.question: Why should I use a PPO or Premier dentist?
qa.answer:
The best value is expected when care is received from PPO (greatest savings) or Premier network dentists.
• No balance billing: participating dentists accept Northeast Delta Dental’s allowed fees, so the member will typically pay less.
• No claims paperwork: the participating dentist prepares and submits claims.
• Direct payment: Northeast Delta Dental pays the participating dentist directly, so the member does not pay the covered amount up front and wait for reimbursement.

qa.question: How do I check if my dentist participates?
qa.answer: Call the dentist, visit nedelta.com, or call Customer Service at 1-800-832-5700.

qa.question: How are claims handled with a participating dentist?
qa.answer: The dentist submits the claim to Northeast Delta Dental. Claims for covered dependents should be submitted under the subscriber ID number. The member is responsible for paying any outstanding balance directly to the dentist.

qa.question: Where can I see my Explanation of Benefits?
qa.answer: Northeast Delta Dental produces an Explanation of Benefits showing what was processed under the plan. It is available through the Benefit Lookup site at nedelta.com.

qa.question: What if I see a non-participating dentist?
qa.answer: The member may need to submit the claim and pay at the time services are provided. Claim forms are available at nedelta.com or by calling Northeast Delta Dental. Payment is limited to the lesser of the dentist’s actual submitted charge or Delta Dental’s allowance for non-participating dentists in the geographic area where services are provided. The member is responsible for making full payment to a non-participating dentist.

qa.question: Who receives the payment for a claim?
qa.answer: Payment is made to the subscriber unless the state where services are rendered requires assignment of benefits to be honored and Northeast Delta Dental receives written notice of that assignment.

qa.question: Can I get an estimate before expensive treatment?
qa.answer: For costly or extensive treatment plans, Northeast Delta Dental recommends asking the dentist to submit a pre-treatment estimate. A predetermination can reduce confusion and help estimate expected out-of-pocket expenses; it does not replace review of the policy terms.

qa.question: What if I have other dental coverage too?
qa.answer: If a person covered by this plan also has additional group coverage, the Coordination of Benefits provision in the Dental Plan Description determines the payment sequence and extent of payment. Questions about COB should be directed to Customer Service at 1-800-832-5700.

qa.question: What is Health through Oral Wellness®?
qa.answer: The program is included with the plan. It is based on the individual’s oral-health risk and needs, is described as secure and confidential, and is intended to help achieve and maintain better oral wellness. Depending on risk, the member may be eligible for additional preventive benefits. Those additional benefits are subject to the provisions of the Northeast Delta Dental policy.

qa.question: How do I use Health through Oral Wellness®?
qa.answer:
• Register at healththroughoralwellness.com by selecting “Register Now.”
• After registration, take the free oral-health risk assessment by selecting “Free Assessment” in the “Know Your Score” section.
• Share the results with the dentist at the next dental visit. The dentist can discuss the results and perform a clinical version of the risk assessment.

qa.question: How do I get my dental ID card?
qa.answer: Two identification cards will be produced and distributed shortly after initial enrollment. Both cards are issued in the subscriber’s name but may be used by any family member covered under the plan. Future cards will be issued electronically through the Benefit Lookup site at nedelta.com.

qa.question: Is there a mobile app?
qa.answer: The Delta Dental mobile app provides access to dentist search, claims and coverage information, and the ID card.

qa.question: Where can I find the full plan details?
qa.answer: The Dental Plan Description booklet will be provided shortly after enrollment or may be available on the company intranet, if applicable. It describes the dental benefits and explains how to use them. Members should read it carefully to understand the plan’s benefits and provisions.

qa.question: Who is eligible for the dental plan?
qa.answer:
• The employee/member is eligible.
• A spouse is eligible; a Civil Union Partner is included where applicable under state law.
• Children are eligible through age 26, regardless of student status.
• Incapacitated dependent children are eligible regardless of age.
• Domestic Partner coverage is not included under this plan.

qa.question: Do I have to enroll all my dependents?
qa.answer: If one eligible dependent is enrolled, all eligible dependents must be enrolled unless they are covered under another dental program.

qa.question: Does the plan renew automatically?
qa.answer: The plan automatically renews for a new 12-month Plan Year if the premium continues to be paid. Premiums may change annually with advance notice. Either the member or Northeast Delta Dental may choose not to renew upon advance notice. The plan will not renew if this dental program is no longer available.

qa.question: What should I keep in mind when using the dental plan?
qa.answer:
• Confirm whether the selected dentist is in the PPO or Premier network.
• Use the subscriber ID for dependent claims.
• For expensive or extensive work, request a pre-treatment estimate before treatment begins.
• Track the two-cleaning limit across routine and periodontal cleanings combined.
• Track the annual maximum because diagnostic and preventive claims also count toward it.
• For Double-Up Max, ensure an oral exam or cleaning claim is paid and total paid claims stay at or below $500 for the year.
• Review the full Dental Plan Description for exclusions, limitations, exact deductible application, and detailed terms.
• Contact Northeast Delta Dental at 1-800-832-5700 for questions about networks, claims, COB, or eligibility administration.

qa.question: Is this document the insurance contract?
qa.answer: No. It is an understanding guide, not the insurance contract. The actual Dental Plan Description and policy provisions control. The outline itself states that it should be used only as a guideline and that detailed terms, conditions, limitations, and exclusions are in the appropriate Dental Plan Description.
